records.title: Chang’an / Luoyang ⇄ Tianshan ⇄ Zhetysu
records.note: UNESCO dates this network's formation to the second century BCE through the first century CE. The corridor supported exchanges across environments and political boundaries.

records.title: Zarafshan ⇄ Karakum ⇄ Merv
records.note: UNESCO documents routes across the Zarafshan River basin and Karakum Desert to the Merv Oasis. This corridor can be read eastward or westward.

records.title: Iran ⇄ Anatolia and eastern Mediterranean networks
records.note: Iranian caravanserais, Anatolian route documentation and Palmyra provide separately dated western network anchors. The Persian Gulf–Palmyra–Mediterranean link is historically attested. Segment dates and geography matter when comparing the case for transmission.

records.title: Ṭabarestān ⇄ Galilee ⇄ Anatolia ⇄ Tábor ⇄ France / England
records.note: This is Nathan Tabor’s working comparison sequence. A dated cultural or linguistic intermediary is needed for each arrow. The Galilee → Bohemia link is a documented act of naming in 1420. Its existence does not date or establish a surname route through Persia or England.

records.title: Bohemia ⇄ Missouri ⇄ West Indies ⇄ England ⇄ Africa
records.note: Use this as a separate modern institutional and Atlantic research lane. The museum establishes the 1872 Missouri organization. Individual overseas branches and the proposed connection from Bohemian Hussites to Dickson's order require charter or correspondence evidence.
links: Scottish Rite Masonic Museum & Library · International Order of Twelve

records.title: Ribāṭ, caravanserai and camp vocabulary
records.note: Some architectural forms are comparable, and route infrastructure supported exchange. Track the Arabic term, Persian terminology and the Turkish or Czech camp words separately before assigning a shared origin.
